name: Apollo 8
short_status: Completed Dec 27, 1968: first crewed flight to leave Earth orbit, 10 lunar orbits on Christmas Eve, recovered by USS Yorktown in the Pacific.
tagline: NASA · United States · Crewed orbiter · 1968 · The space race Success
stats: reentry speed, the fastest humans had ever flown
first humans to see the Moon's far side

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 21 Dec 1968, 7:51 a.m. EST, Launch Pad 39A, Kennedy Space Center, on Saturn V AS-503 (first crewed Saturn V)

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: Frank Borman (commander), James A. Lovell Jr. (command module pilot), William A. Anders (lunar module pilot)

facts.label: Translunar injection
facts.value: 2 hours 50 minutes ground elapsed time, a 5-minute 17-second S-IVB burn

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 24 Dec 1968, at 69:08:52 GET; 4-minute 2-second burn into a 70 x 193 mile orbit, later circularized at about 70 miles

facts.label: Lunar orbits
facts.value: 10 revolutions in about 20 hours; first humans to see the Moon's far side with their own eyes

facts.label: Christmas Eve broadcast
facts.value: 24 Dec 1968: the crew read the first ten verses of Genesis; Borman recalled NASA telling them it would be "the largest audience that had ever listened to a human voice"

facts.label: Earthrise
facts.value: Color photograph AS08-14-2383 taken by Bill Anders on 24 Dec 1968, during lunar orbit

facts.label: Trans-Earth injection
facts.value: 89:19:16 GET on Christmas morning; Lovell radioed "Please be informed there is a Santa Claus"

facts.label: Reentry
facts.value: 24,696 mph, heatshield heating to about 5,000 degrees F; the fastest any humans had flown to that date

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 27 Dec 1968, 10:51:42 a.m. EST, Pacific Ocean, about 5,100 yards from recovery ship USS Yorktown

facts.label: TV broadcasts
facts.value: Six telecasts during the mission, carried worldwide in real time to all five continents

facts.label: Crew legacy (as of July 2026)
facts.value: All three crew members are deceased: Borman died 7 Nov 2023 (age 95); Anders died 7 June 2024 (age 90, plane crash); Lovell died 7 Aug 2025 (age 97)

timeline: With lunar module deliveries slipping, NASA re-scopes Apollo 8 as a CSM-only lunar orbit mission to keep the end-of-decade goal alive
Launch at 7:51 a.m. EST from Pad 39A, the first crewed Saturn V; translunar injection 2 h 50 m later
Lunar orbit insertion at 69:08:52 GET behind the Moon; first humans in lunar orbit
Anders photographs Earthrise; on the ninth orbit the crew reads Genesis to the largest broadcast audience to date
Trans-Earth injection at 89:19:16 GET; Lovell: "Please be informed there is a Santa Claus"
Reentry at 24,696 mph and splashdown in the Pacific at 10:51:42 a.m. EST; crew recovered by USS Yorktown
